title: Evolution changes the competency gene more often than any structural gene

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Evolution changes the competency gene more often than any structural gene

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In the 1D artificial embryogeny model with evolvable competency, positional changes to cells over 1000 generations resulted from changes to the competency gene significantly more often than from changes to any of the fifty structural genes.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Cellular Competency during Development Alters Evolutionary Dynamics in an Artificial Embryogeny Model

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Shreesha L 2023, Cellular Competency during Development Alters Evolutionary Dynamics in an Artificial Embryogeny Model › 4. Discussion › 4.6. Where the Hard Work Is Done: An Intelligence Ratchet

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: We found that the competency gene is changed significantly more often over the course of evolution than any structural gene (Figure 6).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Shreesha L, Levin M, “Cellular Competency during Development Alters Evolutionary Dynamics in an Artificial Embryogeny Model”, Entropy (Basel, Switzerland) (2023), doi:10.3390/e25010131; section “4. Discussion › 4.6. Where the Hard Work Is Done: An Intelligence Ratchet”. Scope: In silico 1D artificial embryos with an evolvable competency gene

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2023-competency-12: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.88

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: This is a directly logged model statistic with a clear comparison. The published algorithm permits rapid independent replication.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Log every accepted positional change over 1000 generations and attribute it to the competency locus or each structural locus, then compare frequencies with uncertainty. The competency locus must exceed every individual structural locus significantly.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Mutation and acceptance rules determine the result.

Frequency normalization must account for one competency versus fifty structural loci.

fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.88
analysis feasibility: 0.92
discriminating power: 0.94
operationalizability: 0.98
data existence: 0.72

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The public experiment can plot how often the competency gene changes relative to structural genes, so the reported inequality is re-computable. That inequality does not cleanly mean evolution works on competency more, because one wide-ranged competency locus is not comparable to fifty structural loci without a normalization the claim does not apply. The raw count is testable; the effort interpretation is confounded.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: In the evolvable-competency runs, attribute each positional change to either the competency allele or one of the fifty structural genes and compare change frequencies. A significantly higher competency-gene rate would reproduce the count; similar rates would refute it. The comparison still has to rule out an artifact of the allele's numeric range.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
A competency allele ranging toward 500 can register more changes than a positional gene for mechanical reasons.

Mutation rate and representation are not matched per locus in a way that isolates evolutionary effort.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

discriminating power: 0.52
analysis feasibility: 0.68
operationalizability: 0.86
data existence: 0.85
